newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian Broadcasting Corp Midday Update.
newsitem.headline: Australian Broadcasting Corp Midday Update.

text.p: SENATOR COLSTON MAINTAINS SILENCE
Independent Senator Mal Colston is maintaining his silence over his future plans and the illness which put him in hospital last night.
Spokesman for Brisbane's Wesley Hospital, Ray Crompton, would only reveal that Senator Colston is resting comfortably and it's uncertain how long he will stay.

Meanwhile, the President of the Senate, Margaret Reid, has echoed calls by the Prime Minister, Opposition, minor parties and Independent Senator Brian Harradine that Senator Colston stand down as her deputy.
Senator Reid, who's returned to Canberra from an overseas trip early, says if Senator Colston doesn't decide to stand down, it will become a matter for the Senate.
FISCHER DEFENDS HUMAN RIGHTS STANCE WITH CHINA
Deputy Prime Minister Tim Fischer says China's agreement to begin human rights talks with Australia reflects the strength of the biltaeral relationship.
China has agreed to Australia's proposal for a regular formal dialogue on human rights, to begin later this year.
Mr Fischer says the announcement has nothing to do with news that Australia has abandoned its long-standing support for a U-N resolution condemning China for its human rights record.
He says China's turnaround reflects the good work of Prime Minister John Howard in a raft of meetings with China's leaders.
NRMA SAYS CAR THEFT AT RECORD HIGH
The N-R-M-A is blaming the increase in car theft in Australia, which it says has reached a record high, on the economic recovery.
The N-R-M-A says car theft cost the insurance market more than 800-million dollars in claims during 1996.
The motorists organisation received seven-per cent more claims in 1996 than in 1995, with professional gangs stepping up their activities to take advantage of the high cost of spare parts.
More cars on the roads sparked by the improving economy has also increased demand for spare parts.
Fridays were the most popular day for car thefts, with the most popular target the Holden V-N Commodore.
VANSTONE SAYS UNIS DESPERATE TO CHARGE FULL FEES
The Federal Employment Minister, Amanda Vanstone, has rejected claims by the Vice-Chancellor of the University of Sydney, Gavin Brown, that the full-fees decision was forced on him by budget cuts.
The University of Sydney earlier this week announced it will offer undergraduate places to full-fee paying students from next year.
Senator Vanstone says Australia's biggest universities, including the University of Sydney, have been desperate to get the opportunity to charge full fees.
Senator Vanstone says the Vice-Chancellors have had full fees as their policy since 1990.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
